extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia readers and editors interested in country-level disinformation campaigns
extracted.subtask_description: Creating or maintaining a Wikipedia list article that enumerates disinformation attacks organized at the national level; includes guidance on what counts for inclusion and minimal sourcing expectations for additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of disinformation attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: "Disinformation attacks are media campaigns that deliberately disseminate incorrect information through public media channels and the Internet."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page defines the term and notes typical goals of such campaigns: "In many cases the goal of the disinformation attack is to confuse, paralyze, and polarize an audience." Use this definition when deciding whether an event/campaign qualifies as a 'disinformation attack' for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — national-scale requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "This list is intended for attacks on a national-scale, not for example a local political campaign making claims about a single politician."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include campaigns that operate at or target a national scale. Local or single-politician campaigns are excluded. When assessing candidate entries, prefer those with clear national reach, coordination, or impact rather than isolated/local incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing requirement for non-wikilink items
rubrics_metrics.description: "If adding an item that is not a wikilink to a Wikipedia article, please cite a source."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New entries should be linked to existing Wikipedia articles when possible; if not, a reliable source must be provided to verify the claim. This is an explicit editorial requirement for additions to the list to ensure verifiability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational format — listing by country
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are organized under country headings ("Listing by country").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article's structure groups campaigns by country; editors should place items under the appropriate national heading and follow the existing formatting/section conventions used on the page.
